questions.question: What is the effect of increasing temperature on physisorption?

options.B: It has no effect on physisorption

questions.explanation: Physisorption is an exothermic process, so increasing temperature decreases the physisorption.

questions.question: What is the relationship between entropy and adsorption?

options.A: Adsorption leads to increase in randomness
options.B: Adsorption has no effect on randomness
options.C: Adsorption leads to decrease in randomness
options.D: Randomness is not related to adsorption

questions.explanation: Adsorption leads to decrease in randomness (entropy), i.e., DS < 0.

questions.question: What is the condition for ΔG to be negative in adsorption?

options.D: ΔH and TΔS are not related

questions.explanation: For ΔG to be negative, ΔH should be -ve and ΔH < TΔS.

questions.question: What is the dispersed phase and dispersion medium in a foam?

options.A: Dispersion medium - gas, Dispersed phase - liquid
options.B: Dispersion medium - liquid, Dispersed phase - gas
options.C: Dispersion medium - gas, Dispersed phase - solid
options.D: Dispersion medium - solid, Dispersed phase - liquid

questions.explanation: In a foam, the dispersion medium is gas and the dispersed phase is liquid.

questions.question: What is the Hardy-Schulze rule related to?
questions.explanation: The Hardy-Schulze rule is related to the coagulation of colloids.

questions.question: What is the term for the scattering of light by colloidal particles?
questions.explanation: The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles.

questions.question: What is the coagulating power of an ion dependent on?
questions.explanation: The coagulating power of an ion is dependent on its valency.

questions.question: What type of colloid will be most effectively coagulated by Al³⁺?
questions.explanation: A negatively charged colloid will be most effectively coagulated by a positively charged ion like Al³⁺.

questions.question: What is the term for the minimum amount of an electrolyte required to coagulate a colloid?
questions.explanation: The coagulation value is the minimum amount of an electrolyte required to coagulate a colloid.

questions.question: What is the change in entropy (ΔS) during adsorption?

options.D: ΔS is not related to adsorption

questions.explanation: During adsorption, the entropy (ΔS) decreases, i.e., ΔS < 0.
